A_target.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a set of [[Definition:Sentence|sentences]] of [[Definition:First-Order Logic|first-order logic]].
Then $\Sigma$ is [[Definition:Satisfiable|satisfiable]] {{iff}} every [[Definition:Finite Set|finite]] [[Definition:Subset|subset]] of $\Sigma$ is satisfiable.

B_source.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a [[Definition:Topological Space|topological space]].
Then $T$ is [[Definition:Compact Space|compact]] {{iff}} every family of [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed sets]] of $T$ with the [[Definition:Finite Intersection Property|finite intersection property]] has non-empty [[Definition:Set Intersection|intersection]].

substitutions.topological space: Stone space of complete theories / the space of truth assignments {0,1}^sentences
substitutions.closed set for sentence phi: the set of models satisfying phi
substitutions.finite intersection property: every finite subset of Sigma is satisfiable

derived.nonempty total intersection: a model of all of Sigma

object_map.reformulation: Encode each sentence as the (closed) set of assignments satisfying it inside the compact product space {0,1}^sentences; satisfiability becomes nonempty intersection.

validity_conditions: The space of truth assignments {0,1}^S (S = sentences) is compact by Tychonoff, and each sentence's model-set is closed.
'Every finite subset satisfiable' is exactly the finite intersection property for these closed sets.
Topological compactness then yields a point (assignment/model) in the total intersection, i.e. a model of Sigma.
proof_plan:
Let $\PP$ be the set of [[Definition:Propositional Variable|propositional variables]].
Represent [[Definition:Boolean Interpretation|truth assignments]] as points of $\set {0, 1}^\PP$ with the [[Definition:Product Topology|product topology]], which is [[Definition:Compact Space|compact]] by [[Tychonoff's Theorem]].

For each $\phi \in \Sigma$, let:
:$C_\phi = \set {v \in \set {0, 1}^\PP: v \models \phi}$
$C_\phi$ depends on finitely many coordinates, so is [[Definition:Clopen Set|clopen]], in particular [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed]].
Every finite subset of $\Sigma$ is satisfiable {{iff}} $\set {C_\phi: \phi \in \Sigma}$ has the [[Definition:Finite Intersection Property|finite intersection property]].
